title: Customs Tariff and Exemption Ordinance, 1937
source_id: ע״ר 1937, תוס׳ 1, 183; Knesset legislation database lawitemid 2000972; Wikisource page פקודת תעריף המכס והפיטורין
verified_how: Fetched the Wikisource page. Heading prints פקודת תעריף המכס והפיטורין, 1937 (note the older spelling הפיטורין, not הפטורים); metadata gives ע״ר 1937, תוס׳ 1, 183 and Knesset lawitemid 2000972; last amendment noted תשמ״ו (1986); no repeal notice on the page (its own s 10 repeals the earlier customs duty ordinances). The charging provision is s 3(a): customs is imposed on imported goods at the rates prescribed in the Schedule (התוספת). Section 3(b) gives the Minister of Finance power on classification, including to implement international agreements, and s 5 gives power by order to add to or vary the Schedule. The Schedule itself is marked (הושמטה) - omitted - in the consolidated text.
notes: THIS IS THE INSTRUMENT THAT ACTUALLY IMPOSES CUSTOMS DUTY. It is a Mandate-era Ordinance and it is the charging Act: s 3(a) levies duty on imported goods at the rates in the Schedule. The Schedule is omitted from the consolidated text because the operative tariff is now the Minister's order - צו תעריף המכס והפטורים ומס קנייה על טובין, התשע״ז–2017 - made under the order-making powers (s 5 of this Ordinance together with s 1 of the Customs Tariffs and Excise (Variation of Tariff) Law, 5709-1949). So the charge is statutory but the rates are subordinate: see topic_gaps. Do not mistake the Customs Ordinance [New Version] for the charging instrument - it is the administration and enforcement Ordinance.
